title: Setting the transform of a Rigid Body does not update it in the Physics Server
body:
Original Title: **MultiplayerSynchronizer makes Node flicker between local and remote state. (visually + physics)**

### Tested versions

Tested and existed on:

- v4.4.1.stable.arch_linux (from Arch Repo, encoutered bug while using this)
- v4.5-beta3_linux.x86_64 (from linked download page) 
- v4.0-stable_linux.x86_64 (from linked download page)

The feature was introduced in Godot 4, so didn't exist before then  ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

### System information

Godot v4.4.1.stable unknown - Arch Linux #1 SMP PREEMPT_DYNAMIC Thu, 17 Jul 2025 21:05:29 +0000 on Wayland - X11 display driver, Multi-window, 2 monitors - OpenGL 3 (Compatibility) - Mesa Intel(R) UHD Graphics (CML GT2) - Intel(R) Core(TM) i7-10750H CPU @ 2.60GHz (12 threads)

### Issue description

#### The Game
I have a bare bones multiplayer game (well more a experiment). 
I use the `MultiplayerSpawner` and `MultiplayerSynchronizer` to spawn and sync clients, which works great. The setup is basically like every tutorial on that ever.

With one Exception: I can move with a local player in the world before the game becomes multiplayer. The player is then just replaced by the online version.

I also have four entities (bushes) that I can push around, offline and online
(A `RigidBody2D`, of which the velocity is slowed down by a one-liner).

The bushes have a `MultiplayerSynchronizer` that should keep them synced.

#### What doesn't Work
When the bushes were moved offline, and then the game goes online, on every client it flickers very quickly between the local and the version on the server. I can push both versions, the local stays local, the version of the server moves on the server as well.

#### What I expect to happen
It takes one version (the one with the authority, in this case the one from the server) and overrides all other versions with that one.
No flickering just one synced version of the bushes.

### Steps to reproduce

With the project below, or recreate after description above:

1. Start at least two instances. 
2. Move an physics object (bush) on at least one of the instances.
3. Connect the two instances together
4. See it flicker! (on the client only)
5. Move the different versions of the physics objects

Sometimes the flickering isn't immediately obvious.
On the 4.5 and 4.0 it took a few seconds to set in visibly. 

### Minimal reproduction project (MRP)

[multtest.zip](https://github.com/user-attachments/files/21394600/multtest.zip)
